title: Entire (dashboard)/page.tsx (857 lines) is unreachable — middleware always redirects / to /dashboard
evidence: File: src/app/(dashboard)/page.tsx — 857-line page component serving route /. Middleware at src/middleware.ts:152-154: 'if (pathname === '/') { return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/dashboard', req.url)); }' — this always fires for authenticated users before the page renders. The (dashboard) route group is excluded from the URL path, so this page serves / which is always redirected.
failure_scenario: Any authenticated request to / is redirected to /dashboard by middleware before (dashboard)/page.tsx ever renders. The 857-line file is dead code consuming maintenance burden and bundle analysis time. It has already drifted from the canonical dashboard/page.tsx (different imports, different feature flags like showDailyRecap state, disabled DailyRecap rendering patterns).
fix: Delete src/app/(dashboard)/page.tsx. If a root-level page is still desired, replace it with a minimal server component that redirects to /dashboard via next.config redirects or a server-side redirect.

title: @google-cloud/storage is an unused dependency with zero importers
evidence: package.json:23 — '"@google-cloud/storage": "^7.7.0"'. Grep for 'from "@google-cloud/storage"' across src/ returns zero files. The package is installed but never imported.
failure_scenario: Every npm install and Docker build downloads and installs an unused package (~15MB). Increases install time, node_modules size, and supply-chain attack surface with no benefit.
fix: Remove '"@google-cloud/storage": "^7.7.0"' from dependencies in package.json, then run npm install.

title: serverExternalPackages references @the-convocation/twitter-scraper which is neither installed nor imported
evidence: next.config.js:18 — 'serverExternalPackages: ["@the-convocation/twitter-scraper"]'. The package is not listed in package.json dependencies. Grep for '@the-convocation' across package.json returns zero matches. Grep for 'from "@the-convocation/twitter-scraper"' across src/ returns zero files. X/Twitter monitoring is documented as disabled (CLAUDE.md § X Monitoring: 'DISABLED on main (2026-02-21). The monitorXAccounts() scheduler is gone').
failure_scenario: Next.js includes this in its server external packages list at build time. While it gracefully handles missing packages, it's dead config that could cause confusing build warnings if the package resolution path changes, and it misleads anyone reading the config about what the app actually depends on.
fix: Remove line 18: 'serverExternalPackages: ["@the-convocation/twitter-scraper"],' from next.config.js. Also remove the trailing comma on the experimental block if it becomes the last property.

title: Bare tag instead of next/image — misses automatic optimization, lazy loading, and layout-shift prevention
evidence: src/components/cuts/CandidatePicker.tsx:53: ''. The project already uses next/image elsewhere (e.g., editor/[id]/page.tsx imports Image from 'next/image').
failure_scenario: Getty thumbnail images are loaded at full resolution without Next.js image optimization (resize, format conversion to WebP/AVIF, responsive srcset). On slow connections or pages with many candidates, this wastes bandwidth. The manual loading="lazy" attribute is a partial mitigation but misses the automatic sizes/srcset generation next/image provides.
fix: Replace the tag with from 'next/image': ''. Add 'gettyimages.com' (or the actual CDN hostname observed in thumbnail URLs) to images.remotePatterns in next.config.js if not already covered.

title: Bare tag instead of next/image for top performer featured image
evidence: src/app/dashboard/page.tsx:557: ''. No loading="lazy", no width/height, no responsive sizing.
failure_scenario: Featured images from external sources (WordPress, CDN) are embedded at native resolution without optimization. On the desktop dashboard, this image is always above the fold. Without explicit width/height, it contributes to Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) as the image loads.
fix: Replace with <Image> from next/image: '<Image src={topArticle.featuredImage} alt="" width={128} height={80} className="object-cover rounded-lg" />'. Ensure the image hostname is in next.config.js images.remotePatterns.

title: Bare tag instead of next/image for top performer featured image (unreachable page, same bug)
evidence: src/app/(dashboard)/page.tsx:657: ''.
failure_scenario: Same as CLIENT-02. Additionally, this file is unreachable (see FOOTPRINT-01), so this bug only matters if the page is resurrected.
fix: Delete this file per FOOTPRINT-01. If keeping, replace with <Image> from next/image as described in CLIENT-02.

title: SkeletonText is exported but never imported anywhere — dead code
evidence: src/components/ui/Skeleton.tsx:13: 'export function SkeletonText({ lines = 3, className = '' }: { lines?: number; className?: string }) { ... }'. Grep for 'SkeletonText' across src/ shows only the definition in Skeleton.tsx — zero importers in any other file.
failure_scenario: Dead export adds to the module's surface area and could mislead developers into thinking it's a supported API. Tree-shaking should remove it from the production bundle, but it's clutter in development.

failure_scenario: Dead hook that adds a file to maintain with no benefit. The file:line includes an event listener pattern that could leak if misused, but since it's never imported, it's harmless dead code.

title: formatLastSaved utility is exported but never imported anywhere — dead code
evidence: src/hooks/useAutosave.ts:120: 'export function formatLastSaved(date: Date | null): string { ... }'. Grep for 'formatLastSaved' across src/ returns only the definition — zero importers.
failure_scenario: The useAutosave hook returns lastSaved as a Date object but no consumer calls formatLastSaved to format it. The exported utility suggests it was intended as the formatter for the lastSaved value but was never wired up.
fix: Either remove the formatLastSaved export, or import and use it in the editor page(s) where lastSaved from useAutosave is displayed.

title: export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' is a no-op in client components (5 pages affected)
evidence: Five client-component page files declare 'export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"': src/app/analytics/page.tsx:3, src/app/editor/page.tsx:2, src/app/dashboard/page.tsx:3, src/app/admin/users/page.tsx:3, src/app/(dashboard)/page.tsx:3. The project's own CLAUDE.md documents this: '"export const dynamic is a no-op in client components — never add it there."'
failure_scenario: The directive has no effect when placed in files with 'use client'. It only works in server components or route handlers. It's misleading clutter that suggests the author expected it to do something.
fix: Remove 'export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";' from all 5 client-component page files. For the 3 API route files that also have it (system/scraper-health, system/alerts, cron/analytics, scanner/events, scanner/telegram) those are NOT in my slice but the directive IS valid there.

title: react-icons is a second icon library alongside lucide-react — duplicated capability, added bundle weight
evidence: package.json:51 — '"lucide-react": "^0.577.0"'. package.json:58 — '"react-icons": "^5.3.0"'. Both are icon libraries. 15 component files import from 'react-icons/hi2' (HeroIcons v2). lucide-react is also a dependency. Two icon libraries serve the same purpose.
failure_scenario: Client bundles include tree-shaken icons from both libraries. While tree-shaking mitigates the worst of it, two icon libraries mean two sets of icon components in node_modules, two dependency chains to audit, and a forked convention (new components may use either library inconsistently). React Icons v5 ships ~30MB of icon data on disk.
fix: Audit which react-icons are used (Hi2/HeroIcons outline set) and migrate them to lucide-react equivalents (both are outline-style icon sets with near-identical coverage). Then remove 'react-icons' from package.json dependencies.

title: puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth is installed but the service uses Playwright, not Puppeteer
evidence: getty-worker/package.json:14 — '"puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth": "^2.11.2"'. getty-worker/src/session.ts:6 — 'chromiumExtra.use(require("puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth")());' — applied to playwright-extra's chromium browser. The plugin API happens to be compatible between puppeteer-extra and playwright-extra, but the dependency name and tree are Puppeteer-specific.
failure_scenario: The puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth package pulls in puppeteer-extra and its dependency chain even though the service launches Playwright browsers (via playwright-extra). This works because the plugin interface is identical, but the dependency tree is misleading and includes packages that are never used at runtime. A future breaking change in puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth could break the Playwright integration without warning.
fix: Replace 'puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth' with 'playwright-extra-plugin-stealth' (or verify that the playwright-extra ecosystem has an equivalent). If none exists, document why the Puppeteer plugin is used with Playwright in a comment at session.ts:6.

title: Startup logging confirms presence/absence of secrets via *** vs (not set)
evidence: getty-worker/src/server.ts:159-161: 'console.log(`Getty email: ${process.env.GETTY_EMAIL ? '***' : '(not set)'}`); console.log(`Getty password: ${process.env.GETTY_PASSWORD ? '***' : '(not set)'}`); console.log(`Anthropic API: ${process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY ? '***' : '(not set)'}`);'. While actual values are masked, the '(not set)' vs '***' distinction confirms to any log reader which secrets are configured and which are missing.
failure_scenario: Docker logs or log aggregation systems retain these startup messages indefinitely. An attacker with log access can enumerate which secrets are available (e.g., 'Getty password: ***' confirms a password is set and the service is targeting Getty's editorial subscription). This is low severity because getty-worker runs on internal Docker networking, not publicly exposed.
fix: Replace the conditional logging with a simple count: 'console.log(`Getty worker configured — ${[GETTY_EMAIL, GETTY_PASSWORD, process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY].filter(Boolean).length}/3 secrets present`);' — reports the count without confirming which specific secrets are set.

title: export const dynamic precedes 'use client' — directive placement is wrong (should be after imports)
evidence: src/app/editor/page.tsx:1-2: "'use client'; export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';". The 'use client' directive must be the very first statement. export const dynamic is between 'use client' and the import statements, which violates the convention of placing exports after imports.
failure_scenario: While this technically works (Next.js 14 parses the directive regardless of position), it's a code smell — the directive is a no-op in client components anyway (see FOOTPRINT-08), and placing it before imports breaks the standard module structure.
fix: Remove 'export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";' entirely from this file (it's a no-op in client components).

title: Entire useAutosave hook (130 lines) is exported but has zero importers — dead code
evidence: src/hooks/useAutosave.ts:24: 'export function useAutosave({ articleId, debounceMs = 2000 }: UseAutosaveOptions = {}) { ... }'. Grep for 'useAutosave' across src/ returns only the definition file. Zero importers. The editor pages (editor/page.tsx, editor/[id]/page.tsx) have inline Ctrl+S save logic and never use this hook. DraftRecoveryModal (also dead) would display recovered drafts.
failure_scenario: 130 lines of localStorage draft management code (save, schedule, recover, clear, dismiss) sit unused while the editor pages implement their own ad-hoc save logic. The localStorage key scheme uses 'newsroom_draft_<articleId>' but no code ever reads these keys. This is an entire feature (autosave drafts) that was built but never wired into any page.
fix: Either delete the file or integrate useAutosave into the editor pages (editor/page.tsx and editor/[id]/page.tsx) by calling scheduleSave on each content change, checking hasDraft on mount, and rendering DraftRecoveryModal when a draft exists.

title: Custom Button component is exported but has zero importers — 58 lines of dead code
evidence: src/components/ui/Button.tsx:26: 'export default function Button({ variant = 'primary', size = 'md', ... }: ButtonProps) { ... }'. Grep for 'from.*@/components/ui/Button' or 'from.*ui/Button' across src/ returns zero files. CLAUDE.md lists it as a 'Key Component' but no page or component actually uses it. All buttons in the app are raw <button> elements with inline Tailwind classes.
failure_scenario: The Button component provides variant/size/loading abstractions (primary/secondary/danger, sm/md/lg, loading spinner) but none of the codebase benefits from them. Dozens of raw <button> elements inline Tailwind classes — any design change to button styles requires touching every instance rather than one component.
fix: Either delete the file, or start using it in pages/components. If adopting: replace raw <button> elements with <Button variant="..."> throughout the app, which would also deduplicate repeated Tailwind button class strings.

title: DraftRecoveryModal has zero importers — dead code
evidence: src/components/editor/DraftRecoveryModal.tsx — imports react-icons and date-utils. Grep for 'DraftRecoveryModal' across src/ returns only the definition file. No editor page mounts it. The useAutosave hook (FOOTPRINT-11) that would power it is also dead.

title: ExemplarTab and ExemplarSubmitForm are transitively dead — training tab was never wired to any page

The TabId type in dashboard/page.tsx includes 'training' but no rendering case for it exists anywhere.

title: 9 unused shadcn/ui components (~800 lines) with zero importers — dead code pulling in orphaned @radix-ui deps
evidence: Zero importers for: card.tsx (79 lines), badge.tsx (36 lines), tabs.tsx (55 lines), dialog.tsx (122 lines), dropdown-menu.tsx (199 lines), tooltip.tsx (29 lines), select.tsx (160 lines), switch.tsx (29 lines), separator.tsx (31 lines). Only sheet.tsx, label.tsx, input.tsx, and Skeleton.tsx are imported. Grep confirmed zero importers for all 9 files. The project's shadcn usage note says 'npx shadcn@latest add <name>' — these were likely added during initial scaffolding and never consumed.
failure_scenario: ~800 lines of dead code plus their @radix-ui peer dependencies (@radix-ui/react-dialog, react-dropdown-menu, react-select, react-switch, react-tabs, react-tooltip, react-separator) are installed and bundled. The @radix-ui packages together add ~200KB to node_modules. Next.js tree-shaking would exclude unused exports from the final bundle, but they still cost install time and audit surface.
fix: Delete the 9 unused shadcn component files. Then remove unused @radix-ui/* deps from package.json: @radix-ui/react-dialog, react-dropdown-menu, react-select, react-switch, react-tabs, react-tooltip, react-separator. Keep @radix-ui/react-label (used by CutSearch.tsx) and @radix-ui/react-slot (used by Button.tsx, if keeping it).

title: SparklineWithTrend export is never imported — dead export within a live file
evidence: src/components/ui/Sparkline.tsx:91: 'export function SparklineWithTrend({ data, height = 40, lineColor = '#D42B2B', showDots = true, animate = true }: SparklineWithTrendProps) { ... }'. Grep for 'SparklineWithTrend' across src/ returns only the definition. The default export 'Sparkline' is used by analytics/page.tsx, but SparklineWithTrend (47 lines) has zero importers.
failure_scenario: 47 lines of dead code within a live file. Tree-shaking should remove it from production bundles, but it adds to the module's maintenance surface and could confuse developers into using it when the regular Sparkline is the intended component.
fix: Remove the SparklineWithTrend function (lines 91-138) and its SparklineWithTrendProps interface from Sparkline.tsx.

title: STATUS_CONFIG and STATUS_DOT are exported but never imported externally — dead exports
evidence: src/components/ui/StatusBadge.tsx:3: 'export const STATUS_CONFIG = { ... }'. src/components/ui/StatusBadge.tsx:41: 'export const STATUS_DOT = { ... }'. Grep for 'STATUS_CONFIG' and 'STATUS_DOT' across src/ returns only StatusBadge.tsx — zero external importers. Both are only used internally by the StatusBadge component.
failure_scenario: Exported utility constants that suggest a public API but are never consumed by any other file. Adds to the module's surface area. If a developer later imports them expecting a maintained API, they may get a surprise when the shape changes without notice.
fix: Remove the 'export' keyword from STATUS_CONFIG and STATUS_DOT. If they are intended as a public API for status display, document them in the component's JSDoc.

title: Local StatusBadge shadows the shared component — drifted implementation
evidence: src/components/dashboard/ExemplarCard.tsx:48-79 defines a local 'function StatusBadge(...)' (32 lines) with inline Tailwind classes, HiOutline icons, and hardcoded status text. The shared component at src/components/ui/StatusBadge.tsx uses CSS dots and STATUS_CONFIG. The local version uses different style conventions (icons vs dots, px-2 py-0.5 vs larger padding).
failure_scenario: Any design change to status badges requires updating two implementations. The local version has already diverged in visual style (icon-based vs dot-based). If someone adds a new status value, they must discover and update both places.
fix: In ExemplarCard.tsx, remove the local StatusBadge function and import the shared component from @/components/ui/StatusBadge. Add exemplar-specific statuses (ANALYZED, PREVIEW_READY, PENDING, FAILED) to the shared STATUS_CONFIG map.

title: Date formatting in dashboard uses ad-hoc toLocaleDateString instead of shared date-utils.ts
evidence: src/app/dashboard/page.tsx:284-285: 'const dateStr = new Date().toLocaleDateString('en-US', { weekday: 'long', month: 'long', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' }); const shortDateStr = new Date().toLocaleDateString('en-US', { weekday: 'long', month: 'long', day: 'numeric' });'. src/lib/date-utils.ts exists with nowET(), etDateString(), etDatetimeLocalValue() but is only imported by 3 files. ArticleCard.tsx also defines a local getTimeAgo() function (lines 41-52). Analytics page uses bare toLocaleDateString with no timezone arg.
failure_scenario: Dates render in the end-user's browser local timezone, not the newsroom's ET timezone. The analytics page renders date headers that shift with the viewer's location — a reader in California sees different dates than an editor in New York for the same analytics data.
fix: Add formatDisplayDate() to src/lib/date-utils.ts that defaults to ET and provides presets (short, long, timeAgo). Replace all inline date formatting across ArticleCard, dashboard, analytics, and admin/users pages with imports from date-utils.

title: FastPathError base class is exported but never imported externally — dead export
evidence: getty-worker/src/fast-path.ts:21: 'export class FastPathError extends Error { ... }'. The subclasses (FastPathAuthError, FastPathBotWallError, FastPathHttpError, FastPathShapeError) are imported and used by getty.ts for type-narrowed catch blocks. But the base class FastPathError is never imported, caught, or referenced in any other file — all error handling uses the concrete subclasses.
failure_scenario: Dead export with no consumer. The base class exists for hierarchy but no code depends on catching FastPathError specifically.
fix: Remove the 'export' keyword from FastPathError (keep it as an internal base class).
